ai.name: Martin Alderson / Simon Willison
ai.hook: New detail emerges: Hugging Face's attack surface is 'enormous' by design, not just bad luck.
insights: Executing arbitrary code is Hugging Face's actual product, so the sandbox escape found a target-rich environment
Thomas Ptacek argues **any 2025 open-weights model** with a pentest harness could likely pull off the same sandbox escape
Debate has shifted from 'was this a stunt' to 'why did anyone assume OpenAI's sandbox was sound'
ai.for_you: No direct action for the agency, but worth knowing that self-hosted or open models carry real security exposure if you ever wire client data into agentic pipelines without hardened sandboxing.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Story continued with new technical detail beyond yesterday's disclosure

ai.name: Eiso Kant

podcasts.episode: Poolside's Model Factory, Laguna S, Open Models, and the Race to AGI
podcasts.takeaway: Small, fast-iterating teams with the right experiment infrastructure can beat much larger models.
key_points: Poolside runs **10,000-20,000 experiments a month** with agents increasingly modifying their own training pipeline
Laguna S, a 118B MoE model, beats a ~1T parameter competitor
Kant argues persistence, verification, and backtracking matter more than raw model intelligence
podcasts.for_you: The lesson isn't about model training, it's about iteration speed: your AI agency wins by testing many small workflow variants per client fast, not by building one 'perfect' automation up front.
